title: 20-Minute Turkish Çılbır with Garlicky Yogurt & Aleppo Butter
dek: Soft poached eggs settle into cool garlicky yogurt under warm Aleppo-pepper butter and fresh dill for a fast, budget-friendly Turkish breakfast.
image_alt: Two poached eggs on thick herbed yogurt with reddish Aleppo butter and fresh dill on a white plate
ingredients: 1 cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt, brought to cool room temperature
4 large eggs, preferably pasteurized if serving with soft yolks
1 tsp Aleppo pepper, plus more to finish
2 tbsp chopped fresh dill, plus small fronds to finish
Warm pita or toast, optional, for serving

instructions.name: Take the chill off the yogurt
instructions.text: Stir the yogurt, garlic, 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, black pepper and half the chopped dill in a medium bowl. Let it stand while the water heats, but no longer than 1 hour. Cold yogurt cools the eggs too quickly, while gently tempered yogurt keeps the finished plate creamy and warm enough to enjoy.

instructions.name: Set up a quiet poach
instructions.text: Fill a wide saucepan with 3 inches of water and bring it just to a simmer over medium heat; small bubbles should gather on the bottom without a rolling boil. Stir in the vinegar. Crack each egg into its own small cup so you can lower it close to the water without breaking the yolk.

instructions.name: Poach the eggs in two batches
instructions.text: Slide two eggs into the barely simmering water, leaving space between them. Cook 3 1/2 to 4 minutes for set whites and soft yolks when using pasteurized eggs, or 5 to 6 minutes for firm yolks. For non-pasteurized eggs, cook until both white and yolk are firm or the center reaches 160°F. Lift with a slotted spoon, blot the underside on a clean towel and repeat with the remaining eggs.

instructions.name: Bloom the Aleppo butter
instructions.text: While the second batch poaches, melt the butter with the olive oil in a small skillet over low heat. Remove the skillet from the burner, stir in the Aleppo pepper and paprika, and let them bloom for 30 seconds. The fat should turn brick red and smell toasty without sizzling hard or darkening the spices.

instructions.name: Build two warm plates
instructions.text: Divide the garlicky yogurt between two shallow bowls or plates and make two small wells in each. Set two drained eggs on every portion. Spoon the warm Aleppo butter over the eggs and yogurt, then finish with the remaining chopped dill, dill fronds, a pinch of Aleppo pepper and the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt as needed. Serve immediately, with warm pita or toast if desired.

why_it_works: Tempering the yogurt briefly keeps the contrast creamy rather than refrigerator-cold without leaving dairy at room temperature for an unsafe length of time.
A bare simmer sets delicate egg whites around the yolks instead of tearing them apart in turbulent boiling water.
A small amount of vinegar helps loose egg whites coagulate faster; draining and blotting prevents poaching water from thinning the yogurt.
Blooming Aleppo pepper off the heat protects its fruity flavor while the butter and olive oil spread the spice evenly across the eggs and yogurt.
swaps: Replace Aleppo pepper with 3/4 teaspoon sweet paprika plus 1/8 teaspoon crushed red pepper; the flavor will be sharper and slightly less fruity.
Use 2% Greek yogurt for a lighter base. Avoid thin conventional yogurt unless you strain it in a fine-mesh sieve for at least 30 minutes.
For an easier egg method, cook four 7-minute jammy eggs, chill briefly, peel and halve them over the yogurt instead of poaching.
Use chopped parsley or mint in place of dill, or combine either herb with dill when you have only a small amount.
storage: For the best texture, poach the eggs immediately before serving. Refrigerate the garlic yogurt in an airtight container for up to 3 days and the Aleppo butter for up to 5 days; warm the butter gently before assembly. If firm-cooked poached eggs must be stored, refrigerate them in clean cold water within 2 hours for up to 2 days, then reheat in hot water until the centers reach 165°F. Do not freeze the assembled dish.
notes: Fresh eggs hold a neater oval because their whites are thicker. If an egg has a very watery outer white, strain it for 10 seconds in a fine-mesh sieve before sliding it into the cup.
Use pasteurized shell eggs when serving soft or runny yolks to children, pregnant people, older adults or anyone with a weakened immune system; otherwise cook the yolks firm.
Keep the butter over low heat and add the peppers after removing the pan from the burner. Burned paprika turns bitter quickly and loses its bright red color.
The calorie and cost estimates cover the eggs, yogurt, butter and herbs; optional pita or toast will add approximately 80 to 170 calories and $0.25 to $0.75 per serving.

faqs.q: How do I keep poached eggs from spreading into wisps?
faqs.a: Start with fresh eggs, crack each one into a cup and keep the water at a bare simmer. A short drain through a fine-mesh sieve removes the loosest white, while vinegar helps the remaining white set quickly. Do not create a strong whirlpool when cooking more than one egg at a time.

faqs.q: Can I make çılbır without runny yolks?
faqs.a: Yes. Poach the eggs for 5 to 6 minutes, or until the yolks are firm and the centers reach 160°F. The yogurt and pepper butter keep fully cooked eggs moist, so the dish still works well without a soft center.

faqs.q: Why did the yogurt become watery on the plate?
faqs.a: Thin yogurt or wet eggs are the usual causes. Use thick Greek yogurt, blot each poached egg underneath and salt the yogurt only shortly before serving. If your yogurt is loose, strain it in a fine-mesh sieve before mixing in the garlic and herbs.
